cards.text: The writer of Hebrews has been telling followers of Jesus that under the old covenant only the high priest went into the Most Holy Place, once a year, but Christ came as high priest through a greater tabernacle (Hebrews 9:7, 11). So now the big point: Christ is the mediator of a new covenant. Friend, I couldn't even settle an argument between the dead batteries I shared a junk drawer with, and HE mediates a whole covenant!

cards.question: Christ is the mediator of a new covenant so that those who are called may receive what?

answers.text: A long life in the land

cards.question: Christ died to redeem the called from the transgressions committed under the ___ covenant.

cards.text: Then the writer brings up something from everyday life: a will.

cards.question: The writer of Hebrews uses a will as an example. When does a will take effect?

answers.text: When the one who made it has died
When the whole family agrees to it
When it is read out in public

cards.question: A will needs a death to take effect. That's why even the first covenant was not put into effect without ___.

cards.text: Flashback to Moses, Israel's leader. He proclaims every commandment of the law to all the people, then takes the blood of calves and goats, along with water, scarlet wool and hyssop.

cards.question: Moses has the blood of calves and goats, plus water, scarlet wool and hyssop. What does he sprinkle?

answers.text: The scroll and all the people
The fields and all the flocks

cards.text: ALL the people get sprinkled, so no standing in the back pretending you're busy on your phone that day. And as he does it, Moses speaks.

cards.question: As he sprinkles them, Moses tells the people this is the blood of the covenant God has commanded them to keep.
Besides the scroll and the people, what else does Moses sprinkle with blood?

answers.text: The tabernacle and its worship vessels
The city gates and the walls
The tents of the twelve tribes

cards.text: According to the law, nearly everything must be purified with blood.

cards.question: The writer says that without the shedding of blood there is no ___.

cards.text: So the earthly copies of the heavenly things had to be purified with these sacrifices. Copies get the copy treatment.

cards.question: The copies were purified with these sacrifices, but the heavenly things themselves with ___ sacrifices than these.

cards.text: So where did Christ go? Not into a man-made copy of the true sanctuary.

cards.question: Christ did not enter a man-made copy of the true sanctuary. Where did He enter?
Christ is in heaven now, appearing on our behalf in the presence of God.

cards.text: Now picture the high priest, who goes into the Most Holy Place every year with blood that is not his own.

cards.question: Christ entered heaven to offer Himself again and again, the way the high priest went in every year.
If Christ had to offer Himself again and again, what would that have meant?

answers.text: He would have suffered over and over since the world began
Moses would have sprinkled the people every single year
The tabernacle would have had to be rebuilt in heaven

cards.text: But that's not how it went. Christ has appeared at the end of the ages to do away with sin by the sacrifice of Himself.

cards.question: How many times did Christ appear to do away with sin by the sacrifice of Himself?

cards.text: Then the writer compares it to something every person faces. Man is appointed to die once, and after that to face judgment.

cards.question: Just as man dies once, Christ was offered once to bear the ___ of many.

cards.text: But the writer isn't done yet. Christ will appear a second time, and friend, THAT is why my ovens stay ready.

cards.question: When Christ appears a second time, it will be to bear sin again.
When Christ appears a second time, who does He bring salvation to?

answers.text: The priests who served the tabernacle
Everyone who kept the law of Moses
